findings.title: Embedded-post author links use the opposite lightness
findings.body: This replaces the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with a 70%-lightened primary for the light-theme branch. The corresponding dark-theme branch should use `$secondary` at 70% lightness, not 30%. As written, the author links become much lighter in light themes and too dark in dark themes.

findings.title: Custom-message length color has the wrong lightness in both themes
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but this changes the light-theme value to 30% and uses 70% lightness for the dark-theme `$secondary` value. This both darkens the text in light themes and gives it the wrong contrast in dark themes; the intended pair is primary at 70% and secondary at 30%.

findings.title: Topic-map heading lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: This replaces the original 20%-lightened primary with a 50%-lightened primary, and also uses 50% lightness for the dark-theme secondary branch. The intended dark-theme counterpart to the original 20% primary lightness is secondary at 80%. This makes the heading noticeably lighter in light themes and incorrectly dark in dark themes.

findings.title: Group-member names lose their intended lightness
findings.body: The original name color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but this changes the light-theme branch to 50% and uses 50% for the dark-theme branch. The dark-theme counterpart should be secondary at 70% lightness. Consequently, names are lighter than before in light themes and may have poor contrast in dark themes.

findings.title: Group-member names lose their intended lightness on mobile
findings.body: The original name color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but this changes the light-theme branch to 50% and uses 50% for the dark-theme branch. The dark-theme counterpart should be secondary at 70% lightness. Consequently, names are lighter than before in light themes and may have poor contrast in dark themes.
